title: Sep 12 Results + Sep 13 Preview: Twelve Wins and That Old Tiger Feeling
summary: 80% accuracy on Sep 12 with 12 wins. Detroit's got our attention again tomorrow.

content.value:
## Another Strong Night in the Books

You know, I've been doing this long enough to recognize when the model's humming along nicely. Last night was one of those nights—12 wins against just 3 losses, an 80% clip that reminds me of those stretches in the '90s when certain teams just had your number, except now it's our algorithm having theirs.

The misses? Yankees couldn't hold serve against the Mets in the Subway Series, and the Dodgers stumbled down in Miami. Tale as old as time—sometimes the better team just doesn't show up. But let's focus on what went right, because there was plenty of it.

## The Highlights Reel

Detroit took care of business against the Rockies at 63% confidence—more on them in a minute. The Rays handled Houston at 61%, which never gets old if you remember those playoff battles. Toronto surprised Baltimore, the White Sox took down the Royals, and the Twins edged the Guardians in what's becoming a fascinating AL Central race.

The Cubs and Padres did what they were supposed to do, and even that coin-flip Nationals-Angels game fell our way. When the 50-50s go your direction, you know it's a good night.

## Looking Ahead to September 13

Here's where it gets interesting. We're going back to the well with Detroit, and this time the model likes them even more—69% confidence against these same Rockies. It's a rematch, and if you've covered baseball as long as I have, you know these can go either way. But Jackson Jobe on the mound for the Tigers against Gabriel Hughes? The numbers like Detroit's chances.

I've seen the Tigers go through their rebuilds, their competitive windows, their down years. Right now, they're in one of those phases where the young arms are starting to figure things out. Jobe's development has been something to watch, and Colorado's offense on the road... well, let's just say Coors Field is kinder to them than most visiting ballparks.

## The Bottom Line

When you hit 80% on a Friday night slate, you take it and tip your cap. The model's working, the reads are sharp, and we're heading into the weekend with momentum. Detroit's gotten our attention two nights in a row now, and that's not something I take lightly.

Tune in tomorrow to see if the Tigers can make it two straight, and whether we can keep this accuracy rolling through the weekend. September baseball—it never gets old.

*— Max*
